name: Hidden Gorges
description:
Fri- Sun , October 15-16, 2022

Hidden Gorges, Mt Zero

Image Credit: @Wanderstories

Leader: Wilfred Karnoll 
Rated: Hard. Creek-based off-track, rugged terrain, steep climbs.

High clearance vehicles required. Please indicate if you have this. 

Description:
This trip is  through Private property in the vicinity of Mt Zero, Taravale.
We travel to and camp at the top of Return Creek falls, where we will be checking out Narke falls on the way in.

We drive to Hell hole gorge, explore that and then drive to Button Rock which we will climb, before returning to our camp site at Return Creek. 
If we get time,  we scramble to the bottom of Return creek falls, explore before climbing back up to the campsite.
We pack up camp and return to Paluma by evening. 

All three falls/gorges are very spectacular and Button rock has been called the Mini-Ayres rock, even though much smaller.

We are calling for early nominations including indications if people have suitable 4WD's and space to take extra people. It is what will allow us to work out how many people we can say yes to on this trip. 

We will be limiting numbers as per the wishes of the property owners.

Property Access conditions include:

Proof of COVID vaccination status – double vax minimum.

Restrictions on use (commercial, social media) of photos taken on the property.

What to bring:
Your own car-camping equipment for one night incl. tents, sleeping bag, mat, cooking utensils. day packs, water and meals. Please carry water for 2 days. 

Fees: non-members $5  

We are not collecting RSVP's via form just yet - Please email us info@townsvillebushwalkingclub.com to
a) indicate your interest
b) please let us know if you have a high clearance 4wd vehicle and if you can take a few people with you.

description:

name: Stoney Creek & Wrights Lookout
description:
𝐋𝐨𝐜𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧: Barron Gorge National Park. We will be car camping at Speewah camping area and walk from Stoney Creek car park to the weir on Friday, from Speewah camping area to Smith trailhead on Saturday and from Stoney Creek trailhead to Wrights Lookout on Sunday.

𝐋𝐞𝐚𝐝𝐞𝐫:  Roxana
Rated: 1-5, easy to difficult, from well formed track to uneven terrain, at times unstable, steep and slippery, stairs, creek crossing, rock hopping and scrambling.

𝐃𝐮𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧:  The whole trip will take three days. Walking 1 hour on Friday, 7 hours on Saturday and 6 hours on Sunday.
Distance: 1km on Friday, 9-10km on Saturday, 7.5km on Sunday
Description: Join us for this long weekend at Barron Gorge NP packed with bushwalking. You will need to be self-sufficient for camping and fit for the walks. Please book your campsite at Speewah as soon as you RSVP: https://qpws.usedirect.com/QPWS/Facilities/SearchView.aspx

𝐃𝐚𝐲 𝐎𝐍𝐄 - 𝐅𝐫𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐲 𝟐𝟏𝐬𝐭 𝐎𝐜𝐭𝐨𝐛𝐞𝐫:Drive approx. 380 km (5 hours) from Townsville to Speewah camping area with detour to Stoney Creek for a walk and a dip in the creek.
There will be an optional break from driving for people keen to socialise: meet at 9am in front of the Cardwell pool for a coffee/brunch and walk along the jetty.
Otherwise meet at Stoney Creek carpark at 1pm. Walk an easy 1km to the weir and take some extra time for a dip in the creek.
We will come out of Stoney Creek at 3:00pm, we will leave the car shuttle(s) at Smith trailhead before car pooling and driving the ~30km to Speewah camping area to set up the camp and relax.

𝐃𝐚𝐲 𝐓𝐖𝐎 - 𝐒𝐚𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐝𝐚𝐲 𝟐𝟐𝐧𝐝 𝐎𝐜𝐭𝐨𝐛𝐞𝐫:Walk from Speewah camping area trailhead to Smith trailhead. There are two options for this walk: Djina-Wu/Smith tracks (8.25km, 6-7h, easy-difficult) or Djina-Wu/Smith/Yalbogie/Smith tracks (9.8km, 6-7h, easy-difficult). We will find out on Friday which way people are most keen to go. We will aim to leave the camp at 7am so that we can finish the walk by 2pm and drive the ~30km drive back to Speewah camp.

𝐃𝐚𝐲 𝐓𝐇𝐑𝐄𝐄 - 𝐒𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐲 𝟐𝟑𝐫𝐝 𝐎𝐜𝐭𝐨𝐛𝐞𝐫:
Pack up the camp by 7am and drive the 15km from Speewah camping area to Wrights lookout where we're going to leave the car shuttle(s), then we'll drive another ~25km to Stoney Creek trailhead and walk back to Wrights Lookout (7.3km, 4-6h, easy-moderate). We will aim to be at the car shuttle(s) by 2pm, to drive the 26km from Wrights Lookout to Stoney Creek to drop off people back to their cars. We will then head off to Townsville with an approximate ETA of 8pm.

𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐭𝐨 𝐛𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐠:
Sufficient food and water for three days (suggesting 3-4 litres of water per day)
Water treatment/filtration system for refilling from creeks
Electrolytes, if needed
Sleeping system (e.g., tent, bag, mat, clothes, etc)
Wood for campfire
Sunscreen, hat, & sun-protective clothing - long-sleeve clothing
Insect and leech repellent (recommending Mosiguard which is both natural and efficient)
Shoes appropriate for walking on uneven surfaces
Dry clothes and footwear for after the walk and carpooling
Headlight
Whistle
Any medication you require
First aid kit/snake bite kit & PLB if available
Optional: Camera

𝐌𝐞𝐞𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐓𝐢𝐦𝐞 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐋𝐨𝐜𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧:
1pm on Friday at the Stoney Creek carpark
optional: 9am on Friday in front of the Cardwell pool

Notes:
The group size is limited to 15 people. Because we need to organise car shuttles at the end of the trail for both walks on Saturday and Sunday, please let us know how many people are in your car and if you're willing to use it as a shuttle.
The club recommends that any natural water sources must be suitably treated before consumption.

The fee is $5 for non-members.
You must be over 18 years old to participate.
To register for the walk, contact the club.
To find out more information, contact the club at info@townsvillebushwalkingclub.com.
It's up to the walk leader to accept your walk registration. Club members are given priority at the leader's discretion.
If carpooling, please bring a change of clothes in the car and offer the driver some fuel money.

𝐏𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐬𝐞 𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐝 ‘𝐖𝐚𝐥𝐤𝐞𝐫 𝐆𝐮𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐬’ 𝐚𝐧𝐝 ‘𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐭𝐨 𝐁𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐠’ 𝐚𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐬𝐞 𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐤𝐬
Walker Guidelines - https://www.townsvillebushwalkingclub.com/about/walker-guidelines
Walk Together - https://www.townsvillebushwalkingclub.com/about/walk-together
What to Bring? - https://www.townsvillebushwalkingclub.com/equipment/what-to-bring
Walk Description - https://www.townsvillebushwalkingclub.com/about/walks-description

name: The Cascades
description:
A spectacular mountain creek walk to a great waterfall in the Bowling Green Bay National Park Mt Elliot section. 
Photo credit - @wanderstories
Leader - Keith
Rated – Hard. Full day walk. Suitable for experienced rough terrain bushwalkers. Rock hopping and scrambling up a mountain creek system, uneven footings, tangled vines and  jungle. Scrambling up rockfaces and exposed ledges, some are very steep and high.
Meet – Time 0730, meet point will be disseminated to registered participants.
Must be over 18 years to participate
Non-members (Visitor) fee $5

Water – bring water for a full day walking. Refill from creeks is available, but the club recommends that water resupply from natural sources is suitably treated before consumption).

Contact the club for more information.

name: White Mountains- Canns Creek Section
description:
Oct Long Weekend, 1-3, 2022 

White Mountains- Canns Creek Section 

Image Credit: @amangotree

Leader: Keith
Yes, another trip to White Mountains. This will be trip number four this year for some of us. It is well
worth many trips.

White Mountains National Park - spectacular white sandstone bluffs and gorges and during spring
brilliant wildflowers. Golden-orange, cream and red grevilleas, wattles in all shades of yellow, grass
trees, white clustered ironbark flowers, and numerous other flowers of various purples and other
hues adorn the park at this time of year.

Base trip is three days over the long weekend 1-3 October 2022 Saturday to Monday, with a two day
extension (at least) for the keen (or mad!).
If it is unusually hot, walks may be modified / shortened.

Detailed description - please email us

To RSVP - please email the club at info@townsvillebushwalkingclub.com
